title: Bounded Input Scan Loop
statement: Let $C$ be a family of Boolean circuits, and fix Boolean $\ell_m$ and natural numbers $n,i,B$. Suppose $n+1\le B$. For all natural numbers $d,V,k,U,W$ with $V+d=n$, $k\le i$, $U,W\le B$, and $k+d+1\le B$, the walk initialized in state $nI$ with registers $(k,V,U,W)$ and no result has the following behavior on the input encoding $n$ and $i$: if $k\le i<k+d+1$, it halts with answer $\ell_m$ or the $(i-k)$-th bit of the word consisting of $d$ ones followed by zero; if $k+d+1\le i$, it reaches a configuration satisfying the specified postcondition, with all registers bounded by $B$ throughout the run before reaching it.
